name: Can engineering coordination prevent expensive change orders?

mainEntity.name: Does engineering coordination reduce construction change orders?
mainEntity.text: Does engineering coordination reduce construction change orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: Engineering coordination is one of the best ways to reduce change orders because it identifies problems before crews are onsite. A coordinated set of plans can reveal clashes between framing and HVAC, foundation and drainage, or architecture and structural requirements before those issues turn into field corrections. That matters because construction changes are usually more expensive after labor, material orders, and inspections are already underway. On custom homes and remodels, a single overlooked conflict can trigger demolition, redesign, or delayed inspections. Good coordination does not eliminate every change order, especially when hidden site conditions are uncovered, but it lowers the odds of predictable mistakes. Homeowners should ask whether the team performs internal cross-checks, clash review, and constructability review before construction begins. That process can save both time and money.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. Engineering coordination reduces change orders by catching conflicts before construction starts, when changes are cheaper and easier to make. It helps prevent rework caused by misaligned plans, missing details, utility conflicts, or structural revisions. Fewer surprises in the field usually means fewer cost overruns.
